newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai state oil firm cuts oil business investment.
newsitem.headline: Thai state oil firm cuts oil business investment.

text.p: Thailand's state-run Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) cut its investment budget in oil business by almost two billion baht from five billion baht earmarked earlier due to the current economic slowdown, a PTT executive said on Friday.
Prasert Bunsumpun, PTT Oil president, told reporters that a major cut would be in the area of retail oil stations.

"PTT Oil will cut the investment budget down to around 3.0-4.0 billion baht..because of the economic slowdown and tough competition in retail oil business as there are around 30 players in the market now," he said.
"This affected PTT Oil's profit during the first quarter which amounted to 400 million baht compared with around 500 million baht over the same period last year," he said.
Prasert said the economic situation forced commercial banks to limit credit lines to retail oil station operators.
PTT Oil currently has 1,514 stations nationwide. It had earlier projected to increase the number of retail stations by 150 this year but has now cut the projection down to 100.
